name: Question 14
problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=xy-\operatorname{ln}⁡z.$ Find the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,1,e).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,1,e)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,1,e)+∇f(1,1,e)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-1,z-e⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the definition of $f,$ we have that $f(1,1,e)=0.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x} & =y\, &  & ⇒\, & {f}_{x}(1,1,e)=1, \\ {f}_{y} & =x\, &  & ⇒\, & {f}_{y}(1,1,e)=1, \\ {f}_{z} & =-\frac{1}{z}\, &  & ⇒\, & {f}_{z}(1,1,e)=-\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the gradient of the function at the point $(1,1,e)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(1,1,e) & =⟨1,1,-\frac{1}{e}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the linear approximation of the function $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,1,e)+∇f(1,1,e)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-1,z-e⟩ \\  & =0+⟨1,1,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-1,z-e⟩ \\  & =0+1(x-1)+1(y-1)-\frac{1}{e}(z-e) \\  & =-1+x+y-\frac{z}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Let f(x,y,z)=xy−ln⁡z. Find the linear approximation of f at the point (1,1,e).

a
f(x,y,z)≈−1+x+y−ze
b
f(x,y,z)≈−3+x−y−2z
c
f(x,y,z)≈−3+x−y+ze
d
f(x,y,z)≈1−x+y−ze
e
f(x,y,z)≈−1−x+y−2z
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The linear approximation of the function f at the point (a,b,c) is given by f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)⋅⟨x−a,y−b,z−c⟩.

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (1,1,e) is f(x,y,z)≈f(1,1,e)+∇f(1,1,e)⋅⟨x−1,y−1,z−e⟩.

From the definition of f, we have that f(1,1,e)=0. Computing the partial derivatives, we get

fx=y⇒fx(1,1,e)=1,fy=x⇒fy(1,1,e)=1,fz=−1z⇒fz(1,1,e)=−1e.

Therefore, the gradient of the function at the point (1,1,e) is given by ∇f(1,1,e)=⟨1,1,−1e⟩.

Finally, the linear approximation of the function f is

f(x,y,z)≈f(1,1,e)+∇f(1,1,e)⋅⟨x−1,y−1,z−e⟩=0+⟨1,1,−1e⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−1,z−e⟩=0+1(x−1)+1(y−1)−1e(z−e)=−1+x+y−ze.
